reviewContext.userProblem: Riela SQLite stores grew to about 60 GB for one application (ART) whose real data is small. Memory history (memory_evolution.reverse_delta_json) keeps one prefix/suffix splice per version, so a header change plus an appended item retains 99.6% of a 660 KB document, base64-encoded in JSON (1.23x per version), and history is never retired automatically. The runtime session store keeps the same session JSON twice (workflow_runtime_snapshots.session_json and cli_workflow_sessions.record_json, 12.2 GB each), rewrites the whole session JSON on every save, embeds parent/child copies in workflow_nested_invocations (10.1 GB), protects 387 crashed/cancelled families from prune forever, and never vacuums after deletes. The #179 definition store keeps every version and blob forever (design §1).
requiredOutcomes: One shared VersionedHistory component inside the RielaMemory module (Packages/RielaMemory/Sources/RielaMemory/VersionedHistory) owns codec, table layout, write/undo/redo/restore, retention, pins, detachment and the RFC 6902-style structural diff; memory and workflow definitions only adapt to it (design §2, eh-01).

Retained non-head versions are zlib-compressed binary BLOBs, full or byte splice whichever is smaller, never base64/JSON; content-hash dedupe means identical writes add no version; revision is a monotonically increasing CAS token (design §2.2-2.4, eh-01).

Memory records on VersionedHistory at user_version 7: historyRetention default 2 for ordinary records, 1 for riela/snapshot-store/state writes, enforced in the write transaction; legacy memory_evolution rows stay readable and convert on next write or compact (design §3, eh-03).

Workflow definitions on VersionedHistory at runtime generation 11: default window 10 (0 = unlimited), head / last_file_version_id / session-pinned versions always kept, guarded-delete triggers replace keep-forever triggers, definition_blobs dropped, audit rows deleted only when both version and previous_version were dropped, undo/redo as audited operations (design §4, QA Q3/Q5, eh-04).

Session pins: same-store pin recorded inside the snapshot transaction (recordPinIfNeeded) and foreign-store pin recorded before the local transaction (recordForeignPinIfNeeded) from the runtime store save entry points and the CLI store in-db overloads (design §4, EH5-F3, eh-02/eh-04/eh-05/eh-06).

Session store: canonical header-only workflow_runtime_snapshots, append-only workflow_runtime_executions rows, family-scoped content-addressed workflow_runtime_payloads, nested invocations by digest reference, witnessed fast paths and fences from c1375bcb..a4e2cbfd preserved, bounded bytes per step for a 500-step session (design §5, eh-05).
CLI session records become envelopes over the canonical snapshot, one session copy per session; legacy full rows stay readable (design §5, eh-06).

Abandoned nested invocations: session reconcile --abandoned-after-hours (default 24) marks abandoned_at under acquired locks; retention treats abandoned rows as settled; run-end maintenance is bounded and family-local (payload release + incremental_vacuum) (design §5-6, QA Q1/Q7, eh-07).

auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL for new runtime, message-log, work and memory databases (pragma before WAL), bounded incremental_vacuum after retention deletes; existing databases convert only via the manual reclaimer (design §7, eh-02/eh-03).

Surfaces: riela memory undo|redo, memory show-version --diff-against, --history-retention, memories[].historyRetention, riela workflow definition undo|redo plus GraphQL undoWorkflowDefinition/redoWorkflowDefinition, regenerated SDL, two-store conformance tests (design §9, QA Q2, eh-08/eh-09).

Surface catalog rows, CLI enumerator, help text and docs (evolution-history, memory-history-retirement, workflow-definition-store, session-cancellation-and-reconcile, terminal-retention, storage-doctor-and-compact) with SurfaceParity green (design §9/§12, eh-11).

designDecisionsAndRationale: VersionedHistory lives inside the existing RielaMemory module because RielaCore already depends on that product, so the root Package.swift stays untouched (design §2.1).

Engine runs through a small VersionedHistorySQL executor protocol and never opens databases or transactions, so each store keeps its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and both RielaMemory raw sqlite3 and RielaSQLite can drive it (design §2.1).
Anchors point toward the head and the smaller of zlib(splice) vs zlib(full) is stored, so no stored row exceeds a compressed full copy and reconstruction is bounded by retained rows (design §2.3).
Undo/redo are head moves that bump the revision without deleting; a new write detaches the redo branch (pinned rows kept full, unpinned deleted); restore stays an explicit new write (design §2.4).
Memory uses an external head (memory_entries holds the head bytes) to avoid storing the head twice; definitions store a compressed head row (design §2.2).
Every existing session protects its definition version regardless of status, because rerun of a terminal session loads its pinned version (QA Q3).

Foreign-store pins are written in their own transaction before the local transaction to avoid holding two write locks; liveness checks open the foreign store strict read-only and fail closed (EH5-F3).
workflow_runtime_snapshots is the single source of truth; CLI rows become envelopes keeping generated columns without a table rebuild (design §5).

Payload dedupe is scoped to a lineage family, which is also the retention unit, and old payloads are released synchronously via indexed point lookups so per-step cost does not grow with store size (design §5).

auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL must be set before the WAL switch on a brand-new file, so SQLiteOpenOptions gains incrementalAutoVacuumForNewFile and existing NONE files convert only through the manual reclaimer with a free-space check (design §7).
Large legacy stores convert only through resumable storage compact --apply batches, never on open, so migration cost on open is DDL only (design §10).
intentionalTradeoffs: Definition window only shrinks once old sessions are pruned, because every existing session pins its version (QA Q3).
Run-end automatic work only releases unreferenced payloads and runs bounded incremental_vacuum; whole-session deletion still requires retention config (QA Q1).
Dropped memory version attachment files are left in place and only reported (QA Q4).
Old binaries reject generation 11 / memory version 7 through existing newer-generation errors rather than supporting downgrade (design §10).
Header-only snapshots still carry fanoutGroups/reviewFindings; the eh-05 500-step bounded-write test is the gate.
The guarded-delete trigger mechanism is not a security boundary, only a guard against accidental deletes.
supportedEdgeCases: 660 KB JSON document with a header change and appended item on every write: after 1,000 writes with default retention at most one previous generation remains (design §11).

Undo past the oldest retained version throws nothing_to_undo; redo with nothing to redo throws nothing_to_redo; stale expectedRevision throws stale_revision; dropped or never-stored version throws version_not_retained listing retained versions (design §2.7).
A pinned version outside the window is re-encoded against its new neighbor so it never depends on a dropped row (design §2.5).

25 definition updates leave exactly 10 versions plus pinned ones; a session pinned to version 3 still resumes; manual DELETE outside retention aborts; over-window restore fails clearly (issue C0, eh-04).

Terminal sessions whose pinned version was already dropped are skipped by the pin hook; database paths are normalized (directory to defaultDatabasePath with symlink resolution) for same-vs-foreign store comparison (eh-04).
Legacy inline-executions snapshots, legacy full CLI rows and embedded nested rows stay readable and convert on first save or compact (design §5).
Abandoned-run detection never touches suspended sessions, rows newer than the threshold (recent) or rows with a held lock (live) (design §6).
Partial compact runs leave mixed old and new rows that stay readable; workRemaining signals rerun (design §8.2).
VACUUM conversion of existing NONE databases is deferred with deferredInsufficientSpace when free space is below 2 x (DB + WAL) + 256 MiB (design §7).
outOfScopeEdgeCases: A future in-db caller that first-saves a store-sourced session with a foreign definition store would not record a foreign pin; current callers (WorkStore+Reservation.swift, SpecialistSupervisor.swift) were reviewed.
Legacy cross-store pins that compact cannot resolve fail with definition_version_not_retained for non-terminal sessions.
Linux CZlib linkage is verified only by linux-amd64-build CI after push.
SDL drift beyond the final-gate git diff --exit-code check.
Registry snapshot store retention (WorkflowHistoryStore) and attachment file GC.
